sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker enteric valve architecture (EVA) is of the finitimus type; the species is among the larger ones within the genus (maximum head width WHdW = 1.30–1.42 mm) but its workers are rather difficult to distinguish from those of other species. The soldier EVA can generally be recognized as of the finitimus type; on average its body size ties with I. bulbifrons as the largest among the species with the finitimus type of EVA (head length SHdL = 2.98–3.77 mm), the mandibles moderately curved (left mandible minor curvature SMlc = 0.24–0.36 mm), as in I. planifrons; the head capsule is slightly inflated (head dorsal concavity sagitta SHdC = 0.00–0.07 mm), less inflated than in I. bulbifrons and similar to I. planifrons. The alate on average ties with I. bulbifrons as the largest among the species with the finitimus type of EVA (head width including compound eyes IHdW = 1.62–1.78 mm), but the distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth is generally smaller (IMlAmD = 0.20–0.24 mm), less than in I. bulbifrons (IMlAmD = 0.20–0.30 mm). Morphologically close to I. bulbifrons but with a different distribution: it is at present known only from the north-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (Haut-Uele and Kivu provinces).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule well sclerotized and dark (C6–C7); frontal gland pore concolorous or almost concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus C5–C7, concolorous with the head capsule or one shade paler; antennae C4–C6, without difference between the proximal and apical segments. Pronotum C5–C6, concolorous with the head capsule or one shade paler; meso- and metanotum C4–C6, concolorous with the pronotum or slightly paler; legs C4–C5; wings transparent with a brown to grey tinge (Cf3), the costa darker; abdominal tergites C4–C6; sternites distinctly paler in the middle (C3–C4), darker at the sides (C4–C6), the posterior sternites (C4–C6) darker than the anterior ones. Head capsule with conspicuous setae scattered among the rather dense short fine hairs, mainly near the compound eyes; labrum and postclypeus with conspicuous setae mixed with short hairs; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, most segments with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at the tip (visible above 50×). Pronotum setae mainly on the margins, many short hairs in the middle; meso- and metanotum without visible setae, or with fine pale hairs arranged along the median band (visible at 40×), the metanotum generally with 3–4 larger setae. Legs hairy, the fore coxa with 6–10 fine spines on the ridge and 0–2 ventrally; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with 20–30 spines. Abdominal tergites with setae of mixed sizes; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, together with many long and small setae directed posteriorly. Compound eyes nearly circular; frontal gland pore generally a small elongate mark; ocelli nearly circular to oval, separated from the compound eye by about 0.7–1.1 times the small ocellar diameter. Antennae 16-segmented (the queen and male 5–6 segments fewer through breakage). Labrum domed. Distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth distinctly smaller than in I. bulbifrons (IMlAmD = 0.20–0.24 mm); apical tooth longer and more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 3 marginal teeth, the second expressed only as a slight undulation of the tooth margin between the first and third; only the apical tooth sharp in unworn specimens; the proximal premolar hidden by the molar prominence in dorsal view; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded molar prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth longer and more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 2 marginal teeth, the first sharp-tipped when fresh, the second smaller and blunt-tipped even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, slightly narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe short and very slightly raised; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Wings: R1 completely fused with the margin and sclerotized; Rs single and sclerotized; M and Cu unsclerotized or weakly sclerotized, with 2–3 and 12–13 branches respectively. Measurements: compound eye major diameter 0.43–0.48 mm, head width including compound eyes 1.62–1.78 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.20–0.24 mm, ocellus major diameter 0.17–0.21 mm, postclypeus width 0.77–0.85 mm, pronotum width 1.40–1.63 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule generally C6–C7, paler in long-stored specimens (C5), with a gradient from a darker frons to a paler posterior (e.g. C6→C4); gulamentum concolorous with the head capsule; antennae and labrum 1–2 shades paler than the head capsule; mandibles dark (C8), the base sometimes slightly paler by one shade, generally concolorous with the frons; thorax, tergites and legs paler than the head capsule (C4–C5); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents, the tergites sometimes with a yellow tinge. Head capsule with a few scattered setae; a dense tuft of hairs on the frons surrounds and covers the frontal gland pore; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum always with 5–7 large setae on each lateral lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with setae mainly on the margins. Fore coxa with 1–2 spines on the ridge and no spines ventrally; trochanter generally with long setae in a row, sometimes 2 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with a row of 6–15 spines. Abdominal tergites with the large setae mainly or only on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, often pigmented, together with small setae directed posteriorly. The soldier is on average the largest within the genus. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides mostly nearly parallel, narrowing in the posterior 1/3–1/4, converging more or less from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases; in lateral view the upper margin slightly concave (as in I. planifrons, far weaker than in I. bulbifrons); the frons without a swelling covering the frontal gland pore. Gulamentum in ventral view always more or less narrowing in the posterior half, the anterior half widening at sharp angles and even ear-like at the sides, in lateral view generally flat posteriorly. Antennae 15-segmented. Labrum always deeply forked, wider than long, the sides harp-shaped; the lobes angular, their tips fine, white or semitransparent; the anterior margin concave. Mandibles sabre-like, distinctly shorter than the head, the inner margin smooth, each with only 1 small marginal tooth near the molar area; the surface of both smooth and shining; the right mandible generally slightly more curved than the left. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 57%–63% of the head width, the anterior and posterior margins generally entire. The fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Enteric valve primary cushions (PC) arranged with trigonal symmetry: the odd cushion on average 14% longer than the even ones, generally without a swelling or with a weak one, but the place where the setae abruptly become very dense marks the swelling; secondary cushions (SC) broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum always small, best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with 2–4 small lobes. Measurements: head dorsal concavity sagitta 0.00–0.07 mm, head length 2.98–3.77 mm, head width 2.07–2.49 mm, left mandible ventral length 2.45–2.99 mm, left mandible minor curvature 0.24–0.36 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C1–C3), turning grey in long-stored specimens; proximal antennal segments pale (C2–C3), the apical segment always 1–2 shades darker (C4–C5); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C1–C3); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); thoracic tergites with scattered setae. Fore coxa always ridged, with 1 fine seta, 3–5 spines on the ridge and 1–2 ventrally; fore trochanter with 6–7 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, and with a row of spines. Abdominal tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, often pigmented, together with small setae directed posteriorly. Workers on average among the larger within the genus, but clearly overlapping several species. The fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles). Antennae 14.5 segmented. Labrum domed. Left mandible apical tooth well developed, sharp-tipped when fresh; 3 marginal teeth, the first well developed but blunt-tipped even when fresh, the second weak (expressed only as an undulating tooth margin), the third blunt-tipped; the proximal premolar hidden by the molar prominence; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded molar prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth well developed, sharp when fresh; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller and blunt-tipped even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 70% of the head width. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Enteric valve primary cushions of the finitimus type, with trigonal symmetry: the downstream part of the odd cushion is broad, its bulbous inflation bearing very dense shorter setae; supporting setae generally numerous, 20–38 on each side of the odd cushion; secondary cushions broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum always small, visible in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with short lobes (3–4 small lobes). Measurements: maximum head width 1.30–1.42 mm, distance from the left mandible apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.19–0.21 mm, left mandible functional length 0.63–0.68 mm, mean length of primary cushions 1–6 0.61–0.70 mm, mean width 0.08–0.10 mm, mean length of secondary cushions 0.48–0.52 mm, mean width 0.22–0.28 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index WVPOdd-Elg = 6.54–9.38.
